claims.text: Engineering a nanoscale multiphase microstructure in a rare-earth-free CrMnFeCoNi-type HEA increases its magnetocaloric response at low applied fields.
Nanoscale magnetic heterogeneity creates locally competing magnetic exchange interactions.
Spin fluctuations near the magnetic ordering temperature contribute to the proposed response.
Coherent nanometer-sized magnetic domains or precipitates facilitate a reversible magnetic phase transition.
The reversible magnetic phase transition produces a large magnetic entropy change.
The nanoscale multiphase structure supports rapid heat exchange.
The nanoscale multiphase structure maintains low magnetic hysteresis.
The nanoscale multiphase structure maintains mechanical stability.
The cast or conventionally cooled baseline CrMnFeCoNi alloy has a relatively homogeneous microstructure.
Rapid solidification or controlled heat treatment can induce nanoscale phase separation or precipitate formation in the target alloy.
Under a low external field, the heterogeneous magnetic regions reversibly rearrange their spin order.
The low-field spin rearrangement yields a large magnetic entropy change.
Reducing precipitate size minimizes energy barriers for the magnetic transition.
Lower transition barriers limit magnetic hysteresis.
The engineered microstructure maintains thermal conductivity and mechanical load sharing.
Relative to the homogeneous baseline, the processed alloy will have a higher magnetic entropy change per unit applied field below 1 T.
The conventionally cooled baseline requires higher applied fields for observable magnetic transitions.
The proposed effect is restricted to a near-equiatomic compositional window and temperatures near the magnetic transition.
Large compositional deviations or operation far from the magnetic transition will not yield the same effect.
